key_insight: PsyCIDRA combines a guided psychiatric interviewer with a separate diagnostic reasoning agent to better support interactive mental health assessment.
clinical_relevance: This framework may help clinicians and researchers standardize psychiatric interviews and improve whether, when, and how diagnostic hypotheses are proposed.
method: Built a dual-agent system: one agent conducts free-form psychiatric interviews using tools, expert-written skills, and ICD-11 retrieval.
A second agent reviews the completed transcript and summarizes supporting, conflicting, and missing evidence for diagnostic hypotheses.
Compared PsyCIDRA with direct prompting in simulated and human-blinded evaluation settings.
evidence_signal: In simulation, PsyCIDRA improved diagnostic agreement over direct prompting, with 60.5% rank-1 accuracy on 81 held-out cases; in a blinded human study, it matched psychologists on hypothesis-proposal decisions in 79.6% of cases versus 65.4% for direct prompting.
watch_item: Results are based on simulated patients and controlled evaluations, so real-world safety, robustness, and clinical generalizability still need careful validation.
paper_title: PsyCIDRA: A Dual-Agent Framework for Psychiatric Interviewing and Diagnostic Reasoning
